issues.description: The commented example in the template Main.java constructs Seal, Pig, and Goat with two parameters (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), while the exercise UML and the reference solution define animal constructors that accept only a single String name parameter. This mismatch can confuse students about the correct constructor signature to implement and may lead them to implement different constructors than the tests/reference expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template example and the problem statement consistent: either update the commented example in template Main.java to use single-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")) to match the UML and solution, or modify the UML/problem description and reference solution to include the second attribute and two-argument constructors. Preferably adjust the template Main.java comments to use single-parameter constructors to avoid misleading students.

issues.description: The template's Main.java (commented example) constructs Seal, Pig, and Goat with two parameters (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), while the problem description/UML and the solution implementation define constructors that take only the animal's name (e.g., Seal(String name)). This mismatch between the example usage in the template and the intended constructor signatures creates confusion about the required constructor parameters and may lead students to implement incorrect constructors or search for non-existent overloads.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template example consistent with the UML/problem and solution by changing the commented constructor calls in template Main.java to single-argument forms (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle"), new Pig("Doodle"), new Goat("Buttinsky")), or alternatively update the UML/problem to explicitly show two-parameter constructors and provide matching constructors in the solution/template. Prefer the first option to align with the current UML and solution.
